newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin plans regular radio addresses, agency says.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin plans regular radio addresses, agency says.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin plans to start making regular radio addresses to the nation and is working on the text of his first speech, RIA news agency quoted sources as saying on Wednesday.
The presidential press service could not confirm the report.
RIA based its report on informed sources close to the president, who is in hospital preparing for a heart operation. It said the first speech could be made as soon as Thursday.

The 65-year-old president has chosen the radio because it is "the cheapest and most democratic mass medium which reaches even those corners of the country which are not covered by television," RIA said.
State leaders in many countries make regular radio addresses to the nation.
Yeltsin has all but disappeared from public view since late June, shortly before he was re-elected for a second term.
In his short television appearences since then he has often looked stiff and moved and spoken slowly. But he recently started holding more officials meetings.

Yeltsin announced on September 5 that he would have a heart operation and has been in hospital since September 13. Aides say he is working a maximum of three hours a day as he prepares for a bypass operation due in six to 10 weeks.
